observations: Photo 0 and 2 show a metal transmission/transfer case assembly lying on wet ground, still partially bolted to an engine block, with wiring harnesses and a bellhousing visible.
Photo 1 shows the same or a similar gearbox among several other dismantled engine/transmission units in what looks like a parts yard or container of used imports.
A watermark reading 'POSTED ON ... GEARUP INC.' overlays all three photos; this is a reseller/listing watermark, not proof of origin.
No manufacturer tag, part number, VIN plate, or casting number is legible in any photo.
Surface shows dirt, grease, and surface oxidation consistent with a used/pulled unit; no fluid level or leak test visible.
A person's leg/shoe is visible in photo 1, indicating a yard setting rather than a studio or verified teardown bench.

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the transmission ID tag, part number, or casting number
Video of the output shaft rotating freely by hand, or a bench test clip
Photo of the torque converter and bellhousing area showing completeness

response.reason: No photo shows a readable tag, part number, or VIN to confirm this is actually the claimed Jeep Wrangler 3.6L gearbox, and fitment identity is the thing that sets the price for a used transmission, so even a worst-case price cannot be set without that shot.
